ticker_notes.NBIS: 每MW收入有提升空間至2500萬

zh_summary: $NBIS、$CRWV和$DOCN最被忽視的機會之一是它們最終能從每兆瓦AI計算中產生多少更多收入。目前DigitalOcean透過更高價值雲服務每MW產生約2000萬美元，而CoreWeave約1000萬美元，Nebius僅約700萬美元，後者仍在比填充更快地上線容量，而像$META和$MSFT的大型超大規模合約也傾向於較低定價。而隨著這三家預計到2035年接近每MW 2500萬美元，我認為機會超越增加容量，因為CoreWeave改善利用率，而Nebius的Token Factory和DigitalOcean的推理服務幫助它們從相同基礎設施賺取更多。
en_summary: One of most overlooked opportunities for $NBIS, $CRWV and $DOCN is how much more revenue they could eventually generate from every megawatt of AI compute. Right now DigitalOcean generates ~$20M per MW through higher-value cloud services while CoreWeave sits around $10M and just ~$7M for Nebius which is still bringing capacity online faster than it can fill it while large hyperscaler contracts like $META and $MSFT also tend to carry lower pricing. And with all three projected to approach $25M per MW by 2035 I think the opportunity goes beyond adding capacity as CoreWeave improves utilization while Nebius's Token Factory and DigitalOcean's inference services help them earn more from same infrastructure.

name: GonzalesJ
zh_summary: juan_gonzalesP：Brent剛印出$118，10年期國債收益率為4.94%。這種關係以前是相反的。@robin_j_brooks是對的，這是體制轉變。2026年大部分時間油價上漲意味收益率上漲；這種聯繫已斷裂。Brent和10Y的20日相關性降至2024年底以來最低。原因是歐洲；法國10年期為4.96%，為2002年以來最高。引用Robin關於10Y收益率隨油價上升而下降的結構性突破，因歐洲債務危機。
en_summary: juan_gonzalesP: Brent just printed $118 and the 10-year Treasury yield is at 4.94%. That relationship used to run the other way. @robin_j_brooks is correct, this is a regime shift. For most of 2026 oil up meant yields up; that link is broken. 20-day correlation between Brent and 10Y collapsed to lowest since late 2024. Reason is Europe; French 10-year at 4.96%, highest since 2002. Quoted Robin on structural break where 10Y yield falls as oil rises due to Europe debt crisis.
text:
Brent just printed $118 and the 10-year Treasury yield is at 4.94%. That relationship used to run the other way .

@robin_j_brooks is correct in this analysis. This is a regime shift, not a blip.

For most of 2026, oil up meant yields up. Inflation expectations fed straight into the long end. That link is now broken. The 20-day correlation between Brent and the 10Y has collapsed to its lowest since late 2024.

The reason is Europe. The French 10-year is at 4.96%, the highest since 2002. The spread over German Bunds has widened to 159bp, the widest since 2011. French debt-to-GDP is 117%, versus 90% at the last crisis peak.

Bessent confirmed this week that capital is leaving "concerning" jurisdictions and flowing into Treasuries as a safe haven. The US is catching a bid because the alternative is worse.

This is not a resolution of the fiscal problem. Net interest is still above $1 trillion. The term premium is being temporarily suppressed by a flight to quality, not by better US math.

If Europe stabilizes, the bid fades. If Europe cracks, the bid deepens.

text:
Is going public really about the stock price going up?

Dan Held says IPOs give shareholders liquidity and ways to hedge, and calls it disappointing that Kraken still hasn't gone public

"Kraken, I'm thrilled to see how far it's come from 2019 all the way through today. Coinbase, I think, will always be a little bit bigger, but Kraken is agile."

"I can't deny it's a little disappointing they haven't IPO'd yet. Plenty of companies IPO, and the price goes horizontal for months or years, or goes down. Coinbase is down 50% from the IPO."

"Public markets simply means that the price is actively traded, employees get liquidity, and you can do more sophisticated things like write covered calls, buy calls, buy puts. So it's not really about if number go up."

en_summary: I think one of most overlooked parts of $TSLA and $SPCX is how they're already building what could become one massive AI infrastructure ecosystem. SpaceX and xAI have already bought ~$1B of Tesla products including ~$699M in Megapacks for Colossus II while they're now planning a ~$17B Terafab with Starlink being integrated into Cybercab and Grok powering Tesla's in-car AI. And when you add Optimus humanoids working across factories and launch sites alongside plans for orbital compute then you start to see what Elon Inc. could look like with Tesla supplying the power and chips while Starship launches the data centers and Starlink connects them.
